traps.learned: Written in 0.5.0 for the Sonnet 5 → 5.5 audit from the Sonnet 5.5 prompting guide, migration guide and Claude Code documentation (#28). In 0.6.2 a Sonnet 5 fallback variable that a project documents beside a `model` already on Sonnet 5.5 is no finding: on the 0.6.1 suite a docs file explaining that pin drew a change (#86).

Written in 0.5.0 for the Sonnet 5 → 5.5 audit from the Sonnet 5.5 prompting guide, migration guide and Claude Code documentation (#28). Its areas became ids of the plan's map in #61 (agents, skills, instructions → memory, rules, agents, skills, commands, hooks, ci), after a graded run missed a planted P13 in a skill that the trap's area did not cover. In 0.6.1 its note stopped treating a level the user saved for Sonnet 5.5 as covering the project, after the Opus 5 → 5.5 evaluation showed a run settling effort on the auditor's own settings (#77).

Written in 0.5.0 for the Sonnet 5 → 5.5 audit from the Sonnet 5.5 prompting guide, migration guide and Claude Code documentation (#28). Its areas became ids of the plan's map in #61 (agents, skills, settings → agents, skills, commands, settings, ci), after a graded run missed a planted P13 in a skill that the trap's area did not cover. In 0.6.2 its areas took memory, rules and hooks, the areas where P02 fires: on the 0.6.1 suite a dispatch recipe in a file imported by `CLAUDE.md` got its P02 finding but no P03, while the same pin in an agent got both, since the traps stage read P03 only where its areas said (#86). Its signal and `applies when` took a line that states a named agent's or skill's effort, such as a routing-table row, after a user's report on the Opus transition (#92): the signal named effort only in frontmatter, in settings and in a settings `env`, so a rule that restated an agent's effort stayed stale when the agent was re-tested. The mirror line fires only where the file it names draws P03 on its own `effort:`, and its note names that `file:line`.

Written in 0.5.0 for the Sonnet 5 → 5.5 audit from the Sonnet 5.5 prompting guide, migration guide and Claude Code documentation (#28). In 0.6.1 its kind moved from re-test to change, typed remove (#64): in the 2026-09-29 capability evaluation a held-out answer key required removing `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0`, every skill run kept it as a re-test by following this trap, and only the plain session with the doc links proposed the edit. The model-config page states outright that the setting has no effect on Sonnet 5.5, so nothing is left to re-test. The setting stays as already decided where the project records that it still serves another model, a Sonnet 5 fallback or an agent pinned to a model where it still turns thinking off, which the page's own exception list supports. In 0.6.2 (#89), the second fragment of the first source's passage no longer occurred on the model-config page, which now reads "a saved `alwaysThinkingEnabled: false` or `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0` has no effect there"; the passage was re-recorded word for word from the page downloaded on 2026-09-30 and the meaning is unchanged.

In 0.6.1 its kind moved from re-test to change for a per-call countdown or budget, which is removed or made rare (#64): in the 2026-09-29 capability evaluation a held-out answer key required that edit for a hook adding a per-tool-call budget countdown, and every skill run kept it as a re-test. The guide says outright not to add such a countdown in interactive sessions, while for other per-step context it says to send it less often only where the misread shows, so that case stays a re-test. The inference that a hook's context reaches the model right after the tool results became a passage of the hooks page, and the confidence rose from low to medium.

Added in 0.6.1 as a sibling of P27 (#65). In the 2026-09-29 capability evaluation the calibrated harness held a skill that sends a message to a running agent mid-turn, and the traps stage recorded P27 as not checkable, since P27 covers only Claude API code and is a hand-off. The guide names messages that arrive while the model is partway through a multistep turn among the causes of the injection misread, so the risk also sits in instruction text. P27 stays an API hand-off and this trap covers the instruction areas. It is a re-test of low confidence, since the Claude Code docs do not say where a message to a working agent lands relative to its tool results.
